summary: Satish Chandra was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Allahabad from circa 1940 to 1948. He worked as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University (~1953–1961) and held a post at the University of Rajasthan (~1961–1970).
An Indologist, Satish Chandra Garkoti completed his PhD at Kumaun University between 1988 and 1992. In 2008, he served as Concurrent Faculty at Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Satish Chandra Vidyabhusan studied at Krishnagar Government College, Sanskrit College and University, under Sarat Chandra Das, and earned a PhD from the University of Calcutta. An Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist scholar, he served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (~1910–1920).

Satish Kumar Tiwari, an Indologist and philosopher, earned his PhD from the University of Lucknow (2011–2017). He held assistant professor roles at Lucknow, Ganesh Dutt College, Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University, Mahendra Mahila College, and A.P.B. Government Post Graduate College.

Satkari Mookerjee was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as Ashutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (~1948–1955) and became Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1955.

Working in the fields of Indology and Buddhist studies, Satkari Mukhopadhyaya served as Coordinator of the Kala Kosa Division at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (attested 1999 and 2026).
Satkari Sharma Vangiya was an Indologist and linguist who pursued traditional studies under Ramachandra Shastri Vyakaranacharya (also attested as Ramachandra Sastri in 1970).

Satoru Harada is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973). He held posts at Toyo Bunko (attested 1978), Eastern Institute (attested 1982), and Kokushikan University (attested 2010–2015).
A Buddhist studies scholar, Satoru Noriyama studied under Esho Mikogami. He held teaching posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and Ryukoku University (attested 2003 and 2013).
Working in the field of Buddhist studies, Satoshi Fujiwara was a researcher at the Shinran Buddhist Center (attested 2015) and a lecturer at Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).
Satoshi Hayashima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student at Ryukoku University (attested 2013–2014) and later served there as a lecturer (attested 2015–2017).

Satoshi Hiraoka studied at Bukkyo University under Shozen Kumoi and Takao Kagawa, and at the University of Michigan. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, he taught at Bukkyo University and Kyoto Bunkyo University, becoming president there in 2014.
Satoshi Ito, a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, studied at Waseda University from circa 1980 to 1989. He was appointed professor at Ibaraki University around 2006.
Satoshi Kono is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a doctorate in literature from the University of Tokyo. In 2000, he became a professor at Kogakkan University.

A scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies, Satoshi Naiki earned a PhD from Kyoto University, where he later served as an assistant professor (attested 2016–2020).
Satya Narayan Goenka was a teacher of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Sayagyi U Ba Khin from circa 1955 to 1969. In 1985, he founded the Vipassana Research Institute.

Satya Swarup Misra was an Indologist and linguist who served as Professor and Head of the Sanskrit Department at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and Professor of Indology and Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University (~1974–1995).

Satya Vrat Shastri studied at University of the Punjab and Banaras Hindu University. An Indologist and linguist, he held posts at the University of Delhi (1970–1995) and served as Vice-Chancellor of Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya (~1989–1991).

Satyanad Kichenassamy studied at École Normale Supérieure and Pierre and Marie Curie University. He held positions at the Courant Institute, University of Minnesota Twin Cities, University of Reims Champagne-Ardenne (1998), and Paris Sciences et Lettres University (2023–2026).

Satyendra Nath Bose studied at Presidency University and the University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He taught physics at the University of Calcutta and University of Dhaka, and served as Vice-chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956–1958).
